title: Dual Worker Job Completion Time
statement: Worker A can complete a software documentation task in 10 hours, while Worker B can complete the same task in 15 hours. If they work together at their constant rates, how many hours will it take them to complete the documentation?
explanation: Rate of Worker A = 1/10 per hour. Rate of Worker B = 1/15 per hour. Combined rate = (1/10) + (1/15) = (3 + 2)/30 = 5/30 = 1/6 per hour. Total time needed = 1 / (1/6) = 6.0 hours.

title: Commodity Price Increase and Expenditure Invariance
statement: The price of cloud compute instances increases by 25%. By what percentage must an engineering team reduce its instance running time so that total expenditure remains unchanged?
explanation: Let initial price = P and initial consumption = C, so expenditure E = P * C. New price = 1.25P. For expenditure to remain E, new consumption C' = E / (1.25P) = (P * C) / (1.25P) = C / 1.25 = 0.8C. The reduction is (1 - 0.8) * 100% = 20.0%.

title: Opposite Direction Train Crossing Duration
statement: Two express trains with lengths of 180 meters and 120 meters are travelling towards each other on parallel tracks at speeds of 72 km/h and 54 km/h respectively. How many seconds will elapse from the moment their front engines meet until their tail ends clear each other completely?
explanation: Total distance to be covered = 180m + 120m = 300m. Relative speed = 72 + 54 = 126 km/h = 126 * (5 / 18) = 35 m/s. Time required = Total Distance / Relative Speed = 300 / 35 = 60 / 7 ≈ 8.57 seconds.

title: Sum of Two Independent Fair Dice
statement: Two fair six-sided standard dice are rolled simultaneously. What is the exact probability that the sum of the top faces is a prime number strictly greater than 5?
explanation: Total possible outcomes = 6 * 6 = 36. Prime numbers strictly greater than 5 within dice sums (range 2..12) are 7 and 11. Outcomes summing to 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) = 6 pairs. Outcomes summing to 11: (5,6), (6,5) = 2 pairs. Total favorable outcomes = 6 + 2 = 8. Probability = 8/36 = 2/9.

title: Circular Round Table Seating with Adjacency Restriction
statement: In how many distinct ways can 6 executives be seated around a circular conference table such that two specific executives, Alice and Bob, never sit immediately next to each other?
explanation: Total unrestricted circular arrangements of 6 people = (6 - 1)! = 5! = 120. Arrangements where Alice and Bob sit together: treat (Alice, Bob) as a single unit, giving 5 circular units arranged in (5 - 1)! = 4! = 24 ways. Alice and Bob can swap internal seats in 2! = 2 ways, so adjacent arrangements = 24 * 2 = 48. Arrangements where they are NOT adjacent = 120 - 48 = 72.
